origin.handbackReportText:
DONE. Fix commit ce9d2eb (a separate commit, not an amend). It fixes the missing newline at the end of a tail block's last line.

**Fix:** in `tail_block` of `skills/executing-dag-plans/verify-tests`, the `sed` filter is replaced by `awk '{ sub(/\r$/, ""); print "  | " $0 }'`. awk always ends the line, and the optional trailing-CR strip is in the same awk call.

**New case:** "tails: output without a final newline keeps headers on their own lines". The suite ends its last line with `printf "FAIL: g"` and has one not-green and one ok-absent entry, so it prints an after block then a before block. The case asserts that both headers stay on their own lines and that stdout's final byte is `\n`.

**Full suite after the fix:** `bash tests/verify-tests/verify-tests.test.sh` ended with `RESULT: 41 passed, 0 failed` and exit 0.

**RED-THEN-GREEN:** before the fix, the suite gave `RESULT: 40 passed, 1 failed`. The failing case was:

`FAIL: tails: output without a final newline keeps headers on their own lines (expected [--- t/nonl.test.sh (after) / | PASS: n / | FAIL: g / --- t/nonl.test.sh (before) / | FAIL: g:\n] got [--- t/nonl.test.sh (after) / | PASS: n / | FAIL: g--- t/nonl.test.sh (before) ...`

After the fix the case passes.

**Concerns:**
- I tried `pkill -f verify-tests.test.sh` to stop my own earlier red run, and the permission system denied it. I did not retry. That earlier run finished by itself and then I ran the clean full suite.
- The earlier red run's signal section picked up the fixed script partway through, but the red result above was already recorded.

result:
The plan run is finished: all 16 tasks are done, with none failed or skipped. This session resumed it with 14 already done and finished the last two.

- **`task-verify-tests`** (`4edf9fa`): `verify-tests` now runs each named test case before and after the task's change and labels it, for example `ok` (failed before, passes after) or `not-red` (already passed before the change). It runs the tests in separate temporary checkouts, so your working tree is untouched. Both reviewers approved it on the first pass.
- **`task-verify-tail`** (`893c40f` and the fix `ce9d2eb`): after each failing label, `verify-tests` now prints the last 20 lines of the test run behind it. The quality reviewer found one bug: if a test's last output line had no newline, the next block's header was joined onto it. One fix round corrected it and added a test for it, and both reviewers then approved.

**Tests:** the implementer's final run of `tests/verify-tests/verify-tests.test.sh` reported 41 passed, 0 failed. The reviewers read the code but didn't re-run the suite, and I haven't run any of the suites myself either. The full loop takes over 20 minutes on this machine; tell me if you want it run before merging. The awk code was only checked under gawk, because mawk and busybox awk aren't installed here.

**Needs a follow-up edit:** `skills/executing-dag-plans/SKILL.md` still says `verify-tests` takes "about 85 s per run". On this repo one run took 1405 s, well over the plan's limit of about 540 s. The machine was heavily loaded, so the true figure may be lower, but the line should be corrected. That task is already done, so `/update` can't change it; it needs a normal edit.

**Bash tool timeout:** a timeout in the Bash tool sends no signal to the command. It moves the command to the background and lets it finish. So a timeout won't cut `verify-tests` short or leave temporary files behind.

**One denied command:** the implementer tried `pkill -f verify-tests.test.sh` to stop its own earlier test run, and the permission system blocked it. It didn't retry, and the run finished on its own. Nothing was left behind: no leftover checkouts from this run.

The plan file's status updates are still uncommitted. I didn't commit them because you didn't ask; tell me if you want them committed.
